findings.title: "Water now" is never disabled and has no idempotency: a double click records two waterings
findings.steps: On /beds, double-click "Water now" on a bed (or retry after a slow response). Equivalent API check: send two POST /api/waterings {"bed_id":1} at the same time.
findings.actual: Two waterings are recorded. The button has no :disabled binding, wateringBedId only changes its label, and the server has no dedupe or idempotency key.
findings.evidence: Two concurrent POSTs returned id 5 and id 6, both North bed with watered_at 2026-11-12 10:59:39, and both appear in GET /api/waterings. In beds.vue the Water now button has only @click="waterNow(bed)".

findings.title: Watering saved but reported as failed when the follow-up beds refresh fails, so the user retries and creates a duplicate
findings.steps: Click Water now (or Save watering) while the POST succeeds but the GET /beds refresh fails or times out.
findings.expected: The page says the watering was recorded and offers a way to reload the list.
findings.actual: The POST and refresh() share one try block, so a refresh failure shows 'Could not record the watering.' and keeps the past form open. Saving again records a second watering.
findings.evidence: beds.vue: try { await api('/waterings', POST); await refresh(); return true } catch { waterError = 'Could not record the watering.' }

findings.title: New requests have no timeout; a hung server leaves 'Watering…'/'Saving…' and 'Loading waterings…' on screen indefinitely
findings.steps: Make the API hang (accept the connection but never respond), then click Water now or open /waterings.
findings.expected: The request fails after 10 seconds and shows an error with a retry.
findings.actual: useApiClient and useApiFetch set no timeout, so the request waits until the browser gives up.
findings.evidence: composables/useApi.ts: $fetch.create({...}) and useFetch(...) set no timeout option.

findings.title: Recent waterings on the dashboard and the Waterings page have no retry when loading fails
findings.steps: Open the dashboard or /waterings while GET /api/waterings fails, then bring the server back.
findings.expected: The error state has a Retry button that reloads the data without a page reload.
findings.actual: Only an AlertMessage is shown. The dashboard does not even keep the refresh function (const { data, error } = wateringsResult), and /waterings has no retry button. The only way to recover is a full page reload.
findings.evidence: index.vue destructures only data and error for wateringsResult; waterings.vue renders <AlertMessage v-if="wateringsError"> with no action.

findings.title: When the beds list fails to load, the Waterings bed filter silently shows only 'All beds'
findings.expected: An error explains that the beds could not be loaded and offers a retry.
findings.actual: The error from bedsResult is ignored and the select renders `beds ?? []`, i.e. an empty choice list with no explanation. A ?bed= deep link shows a blank selected option.
findings.evidence: waterings.vue: const { data: beds } = bedsResult; v-for="bed in beds ?? []".

findings.title: Stale or failed list shown together with an error, and a late filter response can overwrite a newer one
findings.steps: Change the bed filter quickly between beds on a slow network, or change it while the request fails.
findings.expected: The newest filter's results are shown, and an error does not leave the previous bed's rows looking current.
findings.actual: If the refetch fails, the error shows above the previous rows, which still render (v-if on waterings, not on the error). Rows for another bed then appear under the new filter.
findings.evidence: waterings.vue renders the table whenever waterings.length, independent of wateringsError.

findings.title: Huge bed_id or watering id returns 500 instead of 4xx
findings.evidence: All three requests returned HTTP 500 'Internal Server Error'.

findings.title: Body containing a raw NaN litres value causes a 500
findings.evidence: curl returned 'Internal Server Error 500'. Other endpoints behave the same, so the app-wide handler is the root cause, but the new endpoint inherits it.

findings.title: Tiny litre amounts are accepted but displayed as '0 L'; absurd dates such as year 0001 are accepted
findings.where: Beds past-watering form, POST /api/waterings, watering lists
findings.steps: Record a past watering with litres 0.0000001, or with watered_on 0001-01-01.
findings.expected: Either refuse the value with a reason, or show it as entered.
findings.actual: Server returns 201. formatLitres rounds to 2 decimals, so the amount shows as '0 L'. Year 0001 is stored and becomes the oldest entry.
findings.evidence: POST litres 1e-7 -> 201 and stored litres 1e-07; POST watered_on 0001-01-01 -> 201 (test rows deleted afterwards).

findings.title: Future-date check uses the server's date, the date picker uses the browser's, and 'Water now' mixes server-local date with UTC time
findings.steps: Use the app from a time zone ahead of the server's and record a past watering for today (the default value), shortly after local midnight.
findings.expected: Today's date is accepted, and dates sort the same way as the times shown.
findings.actual: The server's date.today() rejects it with 'Watering date cannot be in the future.' 'Water now' stores watered_on as the server-local date and watered_at in UTC, so the stored day can differ from the displayed day and ordering against past entries can be wrong.
findings.evidence: schemas.py not_in_future uses date.today(); waterings.py uses now.astimezone().date() for watered_on but UTC for watered_at; the frontend default is todayIso() (browser local).

findings.title: Water now button shows no busy state while the past-watering form for the same bed is open
findings.steps: Open 'Record past watering' on a bed, then click 'Water now' on that bed.
findings.expected: The button shows 'Watering…' and is disabled.
findings.actual: The label condition `pastFormBedId !== bed.id` keeps it reading 'Water now', so repeated clicks each record another watering.
findings.evidence: beds.vue label: wateringBedId === bed.id && pastFormBedId !== bed.id ? 'Watering…' : 'Water now'
